classification.description: Maintenance and repair of data network equipment

tender.description: The University is seeking to procure an ongoing managed maintenance service for its two Data Centres located at Butts Wynd (St Andrews) and Eden Campus (Guardbridge) that ensures all the individual services (power, cooling, fire, security, BMS) are working together as one holistic system.

lots.description:
The University is seeking to procure an ongoing managed maintenance service for its two Data Centres located at Butts Wynd (St Andrews) and Eden Campus (Guardbridge) that ensures all the individual services (power, cooling, fire, security, BMS) are working together as one holistic system.
The Managed Maintenance Service will commence on 1st April 2027 for the Butts Wynd data Centre. The Eden Campus Data Centre is currently being operated under a Design, Build, Maintain & Operate warranty period during its 1st year in operation and as such this Data Centre’s maintenance service support will start on 1st August 2027.
The Butts Wynd Data Centre incorporates 24 server cabinets and is connected to two of the University’s separately routed fibre network installations. The Eden Campus Data Centre incorporates 8 Cabinets. The Data Centres operate based on TIA ‘tier III’ principles and are an essential business critical facility, providing high-quality accommodation for the University’s main servers and storage systems and it is essential that it is kept functional, highly available and secure at all times. Additional information: All tenders for the University of St Andrews are administered through our eTendering System (InTend).To Express an Interest please go to our tender website at https://intendhost.co.uk/universityofstandrews
Please note that 'Notes of Interest' placed via PCS (Public Contracts Scotland) are not automatically accepted

tender.reviewDetails:
The University of St Andrews will incorporate a minimum of 10 calendar day standstill period at the point of information on the award of the contract being communicated to tenderers. This period allows unsuccessful tenderers to seek further debriefing from the contracting authority before the contract is entered into. Applicants have 2 working days from the notification of the award decision to request additional debriefing and that information has to be provided a minimum of 3 working days before the expiry of the standstill period. Such additional information should be requested from The University of St Andrews.
If an appeal regarding the award of contract has not been successfully resolved The Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2012 provide for aggrieved parties who have been harmed or are at risk of harm by a breach of the rule to take action in the Sheriff Court or Court of Session.
The anticipated review body in such cases would be:
Dundee Sheriff Court
6 West Bell Street
Dundee
DD1 9AD
Telephone: +44 1382 229 961
Anyone bringing court proceedings against the University of St Andrews must inform the University of St Andrews in advance of the alleged breach and its intention to bring proceedings. Any such action must be brought within 15 days of the date on which a decision is sent to them or published to challenge that decision.
Proceedings seeking an ineffectiveness order must be brought within 30 days of the publication of the contract award notice in the OJEU, or 30 days from the date of a decision letter to all tenderers concerned, and any candidates concerned, containing a summary of the reason for the recipient being unsuccessful, otherwise 6 months from the date of entering into the contract or concluding the framework agreement.
Where a contract has not been entered into the Court may, by interim order, suspend the procurement procedure. The court may also set aside a decision or actions taken by the University or order it to amend and document; and/or award damages. However, by express requirement the court may decide not to grant an interim order when the negative consequences of such an order are likely to outweigh the benefits, having regard to a number of considerations.
If the contract has been entered into the Court may, depending on the nature of the breach: make an ineffectiveness order; impose a financial penalty; shorten the duration of the contract; make any other order considered appropriate to address the consequences of ineffectiveness or shortening the duration or the contract; award damages.

tender.title: Telemetry Engineering Support Services
tender.description:
Scottish Water is establishing a Framework Agreement for Telemetry Engineering Support Services, covering the survey, supply, installation, commissioning, decommissioning and documentation of Remote Telemetry Units (RTUs) and associated communications equipment across Scottish Water's water and wastewater asset base, together with reactive telemetry support. Services may be required anywhere in Scotland, so Suppliers must be able to service all geographic areas.

The scope includes, but is not limited to:

- Desktop and on-site surveys of existing and future telemetry installations, including communications surveys (e.g. 4G, SOGEA, FTTP).
- Procurement of RTUs and associated equipment through Scottish Water's mandatory RTU framework, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) prior to delivery to site.
- Supply and installation of RTU associated communications equipment in accordance with Scottish Water specifications (antennas, surge and lightning protection, cable containment, marshalling, relays, signal conditioners, Modbus PLC communications, data gatherers and inter-site comms).
- Programming and end to end (source to screen) commissioning and testing of new and existing plant monitored by the telemetry top end, including hot swaps of live RTUs.
- Decommissioning of RTUs and associated equipment, including safe removal, return of spares and WEEE compliant disposal.
- Production of IO tag sheets, mimics, risk assessments and method statements, commissioning and FAT records, Ready to Go Live documentation and Operation and Maintenance manuals, in line with Scottish Water procedures and a Common Data Environment aligned to ISO 19650.
- Training for Scottish Water Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) support staff on installed telemetry.
- Additional on-site support to Scottish Water E&M teams for communications failures, reactive faults and minor enhancements, and to supplement Scottish Water maintenance teams during periods of high breakdown volumes or staff shortages.

Work will be delivered on assets within Scottish Water's Operational Technology environment, which is in scope of the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations, in accordance with Scottish Water's Telemetry Realisation Process, telemetry procedures and Engineering Specification Section 633 - Telemetry. The Supplier will act as Principal Contractor only and must provide its own base facilities, as Scottish Water will not make premises available.

Call-off contracts will be awarded under the Framework by direct allocation or mini-competition. Scottish Water may appoint more than one Supplier. Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee any volume or value of work.

This opportunity is aimed at telemetry, SCADA, instrumentation and controls and electrical engineering contractors with proven capability in delivering telemetry installations on operational water and wastewater assets, a competent and suitably qualified workforce, and the capacity to respond across Scotland.

lots.description:
Scottish Water is seeking to appoint Suppliers to a Framework Agreement for the provision of Telemetry Engineering Support Services. The Framework will support the survey, supply, installation, commissioning, decommissioning and documentation of Remote Telemetry Units (RTUs) and associated communications equipment on Scottish Water's water and wastewater assets, for both new and existing works, together with reactive telemetry support to Scottish Water's Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) teams.

Services may be required across all of Scotland. Suppliers must therefore be able to service all geographic areas of Scotland.

This notice is intended to help prospective Suppliers understand the nature and breadth of the services so that those with the right capability and capacity can decide whether to participate.

The scope of services includes, but is not limited to, the following.

Surveys

- Desktop and on-site surveys of existing telemetry installations.
- Desktop and on-site surveys for future telemetry installations.
- Communications surveys (desktop and on site) to establish the communications options available for future installations and to document existing communications (e.g. 4G, SOGEA, FTTP).
- Surveys will identify hazards and limitations relevant to the telemetry installation, its function and site access, and will record the location, type and function of the RTU and its associated communications equipment, any integration with control systems (PLC and SCADA), the electrical supply, cable ways and marshalling arrangements.

Remote Telemetry Units and associated equipment

- Procurement of Framework approved RTUs and associated equipment via Scottish Water's approved supply chain. Use of Scottish Water's RTU framework (currently SW20/CI/1285/1 - Supply of Remote Telemetry Units, or any successor or replacement framework) is mandatory.
- Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of RTUs before delivery to site.
- Supply and installation of RTU associated communications equipment in accordance with Scottish Water specifications, including antennas, surge protection, lightning protection, cable containment, marshalling junction boxes, knife edge terminations, relays, signal conditioners (24v / 0-20mA), PLC communication via RS485 Modbus protocol, 230v unswitched fused spurs, data gatherers and inter-site communications.
- Where ancillary electrical work is required, design, supply, installation, testing and commissioning in compliance with BS 7671, the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and applicable UK water industry standards, including relevant WIMES, Scottish Water specifications and Sewers for Scotland.

Programming, testing and commissioning

- Programming of RTUs and completion of the IO and mimic configuration based on Scottish Water design packages.
- End to end (source to screen) commissioning of all new and existing plant monitored by the telemetry top end, including hot swaps of live RTUs and signal additions or modifications, in collaboration with Scottish Water's Telemetry Engineering Support Team (TeST) and Specialist Service Delivery (SSD) team.
- Close liaison with Scottish Water Operations, principal partners and control centre staff to plan and coordinate testing.

Decommissioning

- Decommissioning of telemetry RTUs and associated equipment. Equipment is to be removed from site unless otherwise instructed, with any equipment left in place made safe and labelled.
- Return of spares to Scottish Water where instructed, and safe disposal of removed equipment in accordance with WEEE and other relevant legislation.
- Removal and making safe of redundant power supplies, RTU cards and cabling, and updating of enclosure labelling where existing enclosures are reused.

Documentation and information management

- Production of IO tag sheets and mimics based on the design package provided by Scottish Water or its partners.
- Risk assessments and method statements in compliance with Scottish Water requirements.
- Testing documentation, including commissioning records and FAT documentation.
- Ready to Go Live (RtGL) documentation in accordance with Scottish Water SSD and TeST procedures and standards.
- Operations and Maintenance (O&M) manuals in accordance with Scottish Water procedures and standards.
- Compliance with Scottish Water's Common Data Environment requirements for the SR27 regulatory period (Autodesk Forma), including alignment to ISO 19650, naming conventions, metadata, folder structures, workflows and product data.

Training

- Training for local Scottish Water E&M support staff on the telemetry RTU installed, including anything non-standard or specific to the site, rather than generic manufacturer information only.

Maintenance and reactive support

- Additional support to Scottish Water's E&M department as required for communications failures, reactive faults and minor enhancements.
- On-site telemetry support to supplement Scottish Water's own maintenance teams during periods of high breakdown volumes or staff shortages.

Project management and reporting

- Monthly financial and programme reporting.
- Applications for payment in line with the Scottish Water payment calendar.
- The Supplier will act as Principal Contractor only and will be assessed as such by Scottish Water.
- Working to Scottish Water processes and procedures, including the Telemetry Realisation Process and telemetry procedures that form part of the scope documents.
- A defect period of 2 years.

DELIVERY ENVIRONMENT AND EXPECTATIONS

Telemetry and operational technology

The services will be delivered on telemetry equipment, RTUs, communications infrastructure and PLC interfaces that form part of Scottish Water's Operational Technology (OT) environment, which is in scope of the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations. Suppliers will be expected to work to secure-by-design principles and Scottish Water's OT security requirements.

Standards and specifications

Work must comply with Scottish Water's Standards and Specifications, including Engineering Specification Section 633 - Telemetry.

Geographic coverage and base operations

Suppliers must be capable of servicing all geographic areas of Scotland. Scottish Water will not make premises available for Suppliers to establish base operations, so Suppliers must have sufficient facilities to service the Framework. Same day attendance at mainland sites within 150 miles of the Supplier's Scottish base (or the Central Belt if there is no Scottish base) is expected as a minimum.

Workforce competence

All personnel must be appropriately trained, qualified and experienced, and able to work to industry-recognised health, safety and quality standards. This includes, but is not limited to, CSCS / Electrical Safety Certification Scheme, DOMS, Water Hygiene, Confined Space and Working at Height training.

Working with Scottish Water teams

Suppliers will work closely with Scottish Water's SSD and TeST teams and other Scottish Water framework partners and will be expected to meet defined service levels and lead times throughout the telemetry delivery process.

Work will be awarded through call-off contracts under the Framework Agreement, by either direct allocation or mini-competition depending on the nature of the individual work package. Scottish Water may appoint more than one Supplier to the Framework.

Where work is directly allocated, Scottish Water may consider factors such as resource capacity and competence, telemetry device and site experience, performance, quotation and specific stakeholder or project requirements. Appointment to the Framework does not guarantee any minimum volume, value or share of work. Scottish Water Horizons Limited may also use the Framework where it is an entitled user.

This opportunity is aimed at organisations with proven experience of delivering telemetry, SCADA, instrumentation and controls and electrical engineering services on operational water, wastewater or other critical infrastructure assets, and which can demonstrate:

- Experience of surveying, installing, programming and commissioning RTU based telemetry systems.
- A competent, suitably qualified workforce and the resource capacity to deliver across Scotland.
- The ability to produce high quality technical documentation and manage information in a Common Data Environment.
- Capability to operate as Principal Contractor.
- A strong commitment to health and safety and to working collaboratively with Scottish Water and its wider supply chain.

Full details of the requirements, including the scope documents, Telemetry Realisation Process and Standards and Specifications, will be available to participating Bidders through the Scottish Water e-Sourcing portal (Atamis). Additional information: To access this opportunity, please register using the following link :
https://atamis-scottishwater.my.salesforce-sites.com/ProSpend__CS_PublicLandingPage?SearchType=Projects

tender.description: North Ayrshire Council invites tenders for the provision of a Mental Health Wellbeing Recovery College and Peer Support Service.

lots.description:
North Ayrshire Council is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced Provider to deliver a Mental Health Wellbeing Recovery College and Peer Support Service for individuals aged 16 years and over. The Service will provide a recovery-focused, person-centred approach through the delivery of learning opportunities, peer support, wellbeing activities and community-based interventions.
The successful Provider will be responsible for delivering and developing a Recovery College model and Peer Support Service that supports individuals to improve their mental health and wellbeing, build resilience, develop self-management skills, strengthen social connections and increase participation within their communities.
The Provider will work collaboratively with North Ayrshire Health and Social Care Partnership, statutory services, third sector organisations, local communities and people with lived experience to achieve positive outcomes for service users.
The anticipated contract commencement date is 1st July 2027. The anticipated contract end date is 30th June 2030. The anticipated maximum extension date is 30th June 2032 (this will be at the sole discretion of NAC and subject to satisfactory performance and funding).
Tenderers must agree to accept NAC Conditions of Contract for Health and Social Care Services and NAC Exit Terms and Conditions as the contract will be let on these terms.

tender.description: North Northamptonshire Council (NNC) is reopening their Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the supply of services in respect of Nightly Purchased, Supplier Managed Temporary Accommodation. The successful Potential Provider(s) will be responsible for providing this service and liaising closely with the Contract Manager identified by The Council.

lots.description:
North Northamptonshire Council (NNC) is reopening their Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the supply of services in respect of Nightly Purchased, Supplier Managed Temporary Accommodation. The successful Potential Provider(s) will be responsible for providing this service and liaising closely with the Contract Manager identified by The Council.
In North Northamptonshire, demand for homelessness assistance and temporary accommodation has risen sharply and this trend looks set to continue. To meet the growing demand for temporary accommodation, the Council has become increasingly reliant on private sector housing suppliers of nightly purchased temporary accommodation. 
It is important that the Council regularises its expenditure on temporary accommodation with private sector housing suppliers to ensure its compliance with procurement regulations and legislation, and to ensure the provision of safe and high-quality housing standards for homeless households. This regularisation will occur via the launch of a Dynamic Purchasing System.

tender.title: Provision of Homelessness Services in South Lanarkshire
tender.description:
South Lanarkshire Council require a Provider to provide a range of homelessness services across South Lanarkshire.  This includes provision of:
- Homelessness First Stop Emergency Access Temporary Accommodation
- Homelessness Supported Temporary Accommodation
- Outreach Housing Support
- Out of Hours Homelessness Service
The aim of this service is to help meet South Lanarkshire Council’s statutory obligations in relation to temporary accommodation for households who present as homeless and require emergency access and supported accommodation as well as to provide outreach housing support and an out of hours homelessness service.

lots.description:
South Lanarkshire Council require a Provider to provide a range of homelessness services across South Lanarkshire.  This includes provision of:
- Homelessness First Stop Emergency Access Temporary Accommodation
- Homelessness Supported Temporary Accommodation
- Outreach Housing Support
- An Out of Hours Homelessness Service
The Homeless Temporary Accommodation will require the Provider to meet a range of needs including first stop emergency access accommodation and supported accommodation services.
Supported accommodation may be required to meet the needs of households who require a period of supported accommodation to help develop life skills for independent living.
Both first stop emergency access and supported accommodation will require 24-hour staffing, 7 days a week, including a waking night with sufficient qualified staff at all times to ensure the Service is delivered as per this Specification..
The aim of this service is to help meet South Lanarkshire Council’s statutory obligations in relation to temporary accommodation for households who present as homeless and require emergency access and supported accommodation as well as to provide outreach housing support and an out of hours homelessness service.

criteria.description:
SPD Question 2.C.1 Reliance on the capacities of other entities
Bidders are required to complete a full SPD for each of the entities whose capacity they rely upon.
Bidders should note that if the successful Bidder relies on sub-contractor(s)/consortium member(s) to deliver the contract, the Contract will be awarded to the winning Bidder only as Lead Provider/Lead Organisation. In addition, the winning Bidder and all sub-contractors/consortium members satisfying the requirements in this section shall require to enter into a Collaboration Agreement in all material respects in the form set out at Attachment 5 – Collaboration Agreement (also forming Part 6 of the Schedule to the “Standard Terms and Conditions of Contract” contained in Attachment 7 of this Invitation to Tender). The Council will also be a party to the Collaboration Agreement.
SPD Question 2.D.1 Subcontractors on whose capacity the bidder does not rely
Bidders are required to complete a shortened version of the SPD for each Subcontractor on whose capacity the bidder does not rely.
SPD Question 4A.1 Trade Registers
It is a requirement of this tender that if the bidder is UK based they must hold a valid registration with Companies House. Where the bidder is UK based but not registered at Companies House they must be able to verify to the Councils satisfaction that they are trading from the address provided in the tender and under the company name given.
If the bidder is based out-with the UK they must be enrolled in the relevant professional or trade register appropriate to their country as described in Schedule 5 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.
SPD Question 4A.2 Authorisation/Membership
Where it is required, within a bidder’s country of establishment they must confirm which authorisation or memberships of the relevant organisation(s) are required in order to perform this service.
Bidders must confirm if they hold the particular authorisation or memberships.

SPD Question 4B.4 Economic and Financial Standing
The Council will use the following ratios to evaluate a bidders financial status:
Profitability – this is taken as profit after tax but before dividends and minority interests. If a company makes a profit then it is a pass for this ratio;
Liquidity – this is calculated as current assets less stock and work in progress, divided by current liabilities. If the answer is greater than or equal to one then it is a pass for this ratio
Gearing – this is calculated as the total external secured borrowing (short term and long term) divided by shareholder funds expressed as a percentage. If the answer is less than or equal to 100% it is considered a pass for this ratio.
Bidders must provide the name and value of each of the 3 ratios within their response to SPD question 4B.4.
The Council requires bidders to pass 2 out of the 3 financial ratios above.
Where 2 out of the 3 ratios cannot be met, the Council may take the undernoted into consideration when assessing financial viability and the risk to the Council, providing that the Bidder can supply evidence to substantiate any of the mitigating criteria when requested to do so. The following list is not exhaustive and other criteria may be considered where proposed by a bidder as mitigating factors:
Would the bidder have passed the checks if prior year accounts had been used?
Were any of the poor appraisal outcomes "marginal"?
Does the bidder operate in a market which, traditionally, requires lower liquidity or higher debt finance?
Does the bidder have sufficient reserves to sustain losses for a number of years?
Does the bidder have a healthy cashflow?
Is the bidder profitable enough to finance the interest on its debt?
Is most of the bidder's debt owed to group companies?
Is the bidder's debt due to be repaid over a number of years, and affordable?
Have the bidder's results been adversely affected by "one off costs" and / or "one off accounting treatments"?
Do the bidder's auditors (where applicable) consider it to be a "going concern"?
Will the bidder provide a Parent Company Guarantee?
Is the bidder the single supplier/source of the Goods/Works/Services in the marketplace?
The Council will request submission of and assess the bidders financial accounts, and may use financial verification systems to validate the information provided.
SPD Question 4B.5 Insurance
The bidder must confirm that they have or will commit to obtain prior to the commencement of the contract, the following levels of Insurance Cover:
Employer’s Liability Insurance covering the death of or bodily injuries to employees of the bidder arising out of and in the course of their employment in connection with this contract to the level of 10000000 GBP in respect of each claim, without limit to the number of claims.
Public Liability Insurance covering the death of or bodily injury to a person (not an employee of the bidder) or loss of or damage to property resulting from an action or failure to take action by the bidder to the level of 5000000 GBP in respect of each claim, without limit to the number of claims.

SPD Question 4C.1.2 Technical and Professional Ability
With reference to the nature and details of the services that are the subject matter of this tender, Bidders should demonstrate in their response to question 4C.1.2 that they have held contracts (preferably public sector authority) of a similar nature, size and value to those mentioned in the Specification.
Bidders are required to provide examples that demonstrate relevant experience delivering similar services over the last 3 years. A minimum of 3 examples and a maximum of 5 should be provided. The Council reserves the right to verify any information supplied with the relevant Company/Authority.
SPD Question 4C.6 and 4C.6.1 Technical and Professional Ability (Qualifications)
It is a requirement of the contract that all individuals who will be engaged in the delivery of the contract must be appropriately vetted in accordance with the Protection of Vulnerable Groups (Scotland) Act 2007.
The bidder must confirm in 4C.6, that they agree to submit the PVG Declaration document when requested by the Council.
It is a minimum requirement of this tender that Bidders can demonstrate that where required, staff are registered with the Scottish Social Services Council (SSSC).
Bidders must confirm within their response to 4C.6 that this requirement can be met. The Bidder will be required to provide this information to the Council in relation to the relevant staff who deliver the Services when requested to by the Council.
SPD Question 4C.10  Technical and Professional Ability (Sub-Contracting)
Bidders will be required to confirm whether they intend to subcontract and, if so, for what proportion of the contract.
SPD Question 4D.1 Quality Assurance Schemes
Bidders should confirm that they hold a recognised Quality Assurance Standard e.g. BS EN ISO 9001 (or equivalent - see SPD question for further information).
Health and Safety
A Health & Safety Questionnaire must be completed and submitted when requested to do so by the Council, prior to any award being made. The Health and Safety Questionnaire is included in the attachment area for information only at this stage and doesn't require to be submitted within the Qualification Envelope. Bidders Should confirm that they agree to complete the Health & Safety Questionnaire any other associated supporting documents when requested to do so by the Council.
Technical Envelope Question 2.1.4 Health and Care Staffing Scotland Act 2019 is a mandatory requirement, and this question will be assessed on a PASS/FAIL basis. If a “No” response is given in response to this question, it will be assessed as a FAIL, and your bid will be excluded from further consideration.
